title: api: standardize rate-limit/idempotency/retry-after semantics across streaming & function-calls (openai-compat)
author: Asha Patel
description:
Motivation: Unify our API error semantics so clients (including OpenAI-compat consumers) see consistent rate-limit headers, Retry-After behavior, and idempotency handling across both streaming and non-streaming endpoints, and for tool/function-calling flows. This resolves multiple customer-reported flakiness patterns where clients retried too aggressively or failed to surface a usable Retry-After value for streaming connections.

Summary of changes: consolidated the rate-limit/Retry-After header emission in the gateway and streaming proxy, introduced a canonical idempotency validation path that returns consistent 409/422/429 codes with explicit error_code fields, and added mapping rules in the OpenAI-compat layer so responses match common client expectations. Also tightened streaming error propagation so final error messages (and Retry-After headers) are emitted as the terminal event on the stream before connection close.

Key behaviors implemented: 
- Retry-After: all 429 responses (streaming and non-streaming) now include a standardized Retry-After header in seconds; for streaming connections we emit a final control event that includes "retry_after" in the JSON payload and then close the stream.
- Rate-limit semantics: gateway now uses the unified rate-limiter to compute both per-token and per-route limits; X-RateLimit-* headers are populated for observability and the OpenAI-compat layer also emits "retry_after" and an "error_code":"rate_limit_exceeded" in the JSON error body.
- Idempotency: idempotency-key validation has a single canonical path. Conflicting duplicate requests return 409 with error_code "idempotency_conflict"; malformed idempotency keys return 422 with error_code "invalid_idempotency_key". When idempotency results in a transient capacity issue we return 429 with Retry-After and a clear human message.
- Function-calls/tool-calls: errors from tool/function execution are normalized to the same top-level error schema ("error_code", "message", "details") and streaming function-call events include a terminal error event with Retry-After when rate-limited. 
- OpenAI compatibility: added mapping layer to ensure common OpenAI clients can interpret our headers and body fields (maps to "type"/"param" fields where applicable, and preserves original Redwood diagnostics in a "redwood_meta" field). This is feature-flagged and enabled for the compat gateway route.

Testing: added unit tests for header emission and idempotency outcomes, integration tests that exercise streaming termination with a fake rate-limiter, and an end-to-end QA job that validates OpenAI-compat mappings against a small client matrix. Backfilled a small set of regression tests around function-call streaming behavior.

Rollout: feature-gated on "api.unified_retry_after_v1". We deployed to canary, ran a 48h soak with synthetic clients and saw no increase in 5xxs. Gradual rollout to 100% after approvals.

Notes: this PR touches the gateway, streaming-proxy, api-compat layer, and the runtime's idempotency store. Changes are conservative and preserve prior behavior by default unless the compat flag is enabled.

Review conversation (summary): 
- Miguel Santos (reviewer): pointed out an edge-case where streaming proxy might double-emit Retry-After when upstream also sets header; requested de-dup logic.
- Author response: added de-dup logic in gateway and clarified comments; added unit test.
- Priya Mehta (reviewer): asked for clearer error_code names to avoid collisions with existing clients. Renamed to the canonical names listed above.
- QA: Ran manual tool call scenarios and validated consistent terminal events.
- Approvals: Miguel Santos, Priya Mehta, and Samir Khan approved after minor adjustments.

CI: initial pipeline had a flaky streaming test failure on linux-arm; rerun succeeded. All checks green before merge.

Merge: squash merge into main, post-merge migration step to flip compat flag for canary was executed by oncall.

References: Linear: ENG-3456, ENG-3472; Incident link: INC-2026-02-rate-limit-streaming (context for customer repro).
commits: streaming-proxy: terminal control event for retry_after
compat: map redwood error schema to openai-compat fields
idempotency: single validation path + error codes
tests: unit/integration/e2e for retry-after and idempotency
release_notes: Standardize Retry-After and idempotency error semantics across streaming and function-calls; OpenAI-compat mapping added behind feature flag.
